title: CLO2024.1 New Feature Express: Brand New Features Released to Bring Your Creations to Life!
description:
CLO2024.1 New Features Released!  
This update introduces brand-new features: AI Model Workshop, automatic generation of PBR textures, texture effect presets, as well as updates to the virtual model editor, optimizations to the color matching editor, and upgrades to the automatic recognition module!  
Click the video to explore the new version with CLO technical experts!  

For detailed videos of previous versions, please visit: https://space.bilibili.com/477753185/channel/seriesdetail?sid=864877&ctype=0
transcript:
Hello everyone, the CLOSE 2024.1 version is about to be released.  
The new features have been fully upgraded to make your experience more convenient.  
This video will guide you through the update from the perspective of clothing development,  
including UI updates, file preparation, file editing, design, production, display, and the final one-stop cooperation in Closet.  
Without further ado, let’s take a look.  

First of all, we have optimized the UI.  
One of the biggest changes is that in the main menu at the top, you will now see the options: Produce, Connect, and Closet.  
Therefore, you can directly visit here or upload files to Closet.  
You can upload project files, clothing, or virtual models.  
After modifying a file, you can also upload the updated version.  
If you need to use the Everywhere function and upload files,  
you can find it under the Connect option.  
You will also notice that the Everywhere UI has been updated.  

In the Produce option, you can find functions for coloring, material lists, and code checking.  
In the Material section, you can find the material generator.  
In the Virtual Model section, you can find the virtual model editor and other related functions.  

Additionally, in the library window, we have added a new virtual model file folder named Mantel Human.  
You can directly double-click to import and use it in Closet.  
At present, direct size editing in Closet is not supported.  
You can choose to change the size and gender of the Mantel Human virtual model in the map window on the left.  

Regarding virtual models,  
Connect has also updated some faceless children virtual models.  
You can edit their size in the virtual model editor.  

In the new version, the UI of the virtual model editor has also been updated.  
First, you can single-click and drag the virtual model’s measurement line to the actual line  
to change the measurement position and the measurement value.  
After adjustment, you can right-click to reset the position or reset all positions.  
This way, we can adjust the size by editing these measurement values as needed.  

In the right editor, you can set different types of measurement values to check or hide.  
In the width size section, you can first set a total width.  
For example, set a lower-body size.  
You can also choose whether to set the width value.  
You can link the width value and the measurement value below it.  
Linking means that when adjusting the total width value,  
the measurement values below will be adjusted accordingly to fit the total width.  
Then you can adjust the chest size again,  
making the chest outline more natural and realistic.  

Additionally, you can now control the width of female and male models,  
which adjusts the width between the thighs, making them bigger or smaller.  
In the male model bucket, you can change the thigh width,  
and also change the thigh size.  
Similarly, the male model can drag the measurement line on the body to modify the size.  
Set up the virtual model.  

Next, we can import the costume for editing.  
Select a file from the close-up resource library.  
Right-click to open the previous version of this style,  
and load it into the work area.  

In the 2D window, you can edit the pattern below.  
First, switch to the black and white surface view,  
find the sewing tool in the 2D toolbar,  
then add a seam allowance to the seam.  
One of the updates is that the seam allowance will now automatically be cut into the seam allowance.  
This applies to larger seam allowance types.  

If you want the seam allowance to display different types,  
simply click on the seam allowance shortcut.  
You will see different folding types in the attribute editor’s dropdown menu,  
from which you can choose.  

Next, look at the back piece.  
You will see there is a basic line in the middle of the seam allowance at the bottom of the back piece.  
Therefore, even if you use the seam allowance transfer tool to flip the seam,  
the new seam allowance in the middle will retain the basic line.  

Continue to use the production source order line tool to adjust the bottom,  
divide the panels,  
then use the extension panel tool to extend the back piece.  
The updated extension panel tool can also extend to symmetrical panels,  
which is more convenient.  
Since both sides can only be extended outward,  
it is not possible to change the direction.  
However, you can edit the length of the upper and lower lines separately.  
Click OK to extend the panel.  

After completing all editing and modification operations,  
let’s check the seam allowance type again.  
After the update, we can easily open or close the folding option through the secondary selection window.  
You can also use the shortcut key — the single icon key next to the return key on the keyboard —  
to conveniently switch between folding and seam allowance views.  

After completing the editing and sewing of the panel,  
we can see the seam allowance on the clothing.  
We can edit it according to our needs.  

When selecting the button,  
under the mouse pointer’s width,  
you can see the options to add the face button and the eye button.  
Click to open.  
At this time, changing the size of the button will automatically adjust the size of the eye button accordingly.  

If you are satisfied with the clothes you made,  
you can add them to your model library.  
Open the model library,  
find the group where you want to store the clothing model.  
You will see that the upper right corner of the model library  
now has an automatic label button.  
It can automatically tag the panels in the correct model library.  
If some are missing,  
you can select the category of the component,  
then select the corresponding panel,  
press Enter to return to the cart,  
and quickly set it up.  
Finally, click OK,  
and you can find them in the model library.  

For the remaining models,  
you can also update the style and name.  
Right-click on the component,  
click Edit Style,  
and modify the name and shrink chart.  
Once modified, the original component’s name will be updated accordingly.  

Insert this pleated vest and select the fabric.  
The current clothing type is wool.  
There is a new option below,  
and the bone line is mixed randomly.  
When you enable it,  
you will see that the fabric’s color becomes more random.  
You can control the randomness by sliding the slider or entering numbers.  
You can also use random variables to get different results.  

Additionally, a function to adjust the direction of the wool has been added.  
You can adjust the wool direction by sliding the slider or entering numbers.  

CLO now supports the sRGB format.  
Open an sRGB sticker created by Photoshop in CLO.  
The colors will be more consistent.  
Here, insert an inner top shirt,  
and add sRGB stickers on it.  
This sticker was created in Photoshop.  
Now, the color displayed in CLO  
and the color in Photoshop remain the same.  
Conversely, the sRGB sticker from CLO also displays the same color.  

Next, let’s make jeans.  
A sticker is added to the jeans.  
Select the sticker,  
and you will see that the property editor has added a new option below the line chart:  
Use the same as the plant.  
Click the button,  
and you can apply the hairline texture of the jeans fabric to the sticker.  
After enabling this,  
the sticker also applies the hairline effect of the jeans.  
If you select the jeans fabric and adjust the hairline intensity,  
the hairline effect on the sticker will also change.  

Below this picture,  
transparent picture,  
and other 3D stickers,  
there is also an option to use the same as the plant.  

Additionally, the sticker now has a preset type.  
Click the download menu,  
and you will see the default is digital print.  
Then there are uniform, retrofitting, and gold.  
The gold color can be modified.  
If you choose to mix with the plant,  
the sticker will apply all 3D stickers of the plant.  
You can see that at this time,  
the "use the same as the plant" option is active below the 3D sticker.  

Another update about the sticker is:  
clicking on the sticker in the object window,  
the property editor shows only a texture picture; there are no other 3D stickers at the moment.  
Click the automatically generate button,  
and you can easily and quickly generate other 3D stickers.  
The generated stickers can be stored separately.  
The plant can also use the option to automatically generate 3D stickers.  

Next, let’s look at updates about the color flag.  
We have created a more diverse system,  
allowing you to set more color options flexibly.  
Now, when adding a flag color,  
you can add a flag color that only adjusts the material,  
a flag color that only adjusts all properties,  
or set the flag color information of related materials.  
For example, you can create a flag color that only adjusts the material,  
and modify the color, texture, and size.  
You can also add ink,  
and set the display of the sticker, etc.  
Or you can choose  
to set all material properties of a flag color separately,  
allowing you to modify texture information and physical properties independently.  

By using the new flag color function,  
you can use the above settings  
to view and edit clothes more freely during the workflow.  

The measurement tool in the new version has also been optimized.  
You can switch between different modes by pressing the shortcut key P.  
One mode allows you to change the color,  
and another mode allows you to measure the length of the panel’s outer edge.  
You can operate along the panel’s outer outline,  
similar to the free sewing tool operation.  
Another mode measures straight line length inside the panel.  
You can also create free straight lines inside and outside the panel.  
All measurement values will be displayed in the object window.  

Now you can also more conveniently edit the sticker code.  
When entering the code for the sticker,  
use the edit code tool to select the sticker,  
and in the attribute editor,  
you can choose between a percentage or unit number  
to decide how to change the code size.  
Using percentage numbers means you don’t need to know the exact size for each sticker size, which is more convenient.  

Or use the edit code tool.  
Now you can do inner line refitting on the panel  
to achieve different ways of matching the code.  

When viewing the code,  
we added a full mirror mode,  
which allows you to see all sizes in one image.  
It’s more convenient to observe differences between sizes.  
You can adjust the X-axis rotation to see the garment angles,  
and also adjust the distance between each size.  
This mode can also be used  
to observe the pressure and force on the clothes.  

Finally, you can output clothing rendering images.  
First, open style image rendering in the 3D vertical menu.  
You will now see the chain and components in the style image rendering,  
making the style effect picture of the clothes more complete.  

Next, click on the virtual model.  
Find the sample modifier in the property editor.  
You can now quickly modify the color of the virtual model’s eyes.  
After modification,  
you can click reset or keep the changes you made.  

Additionally, for the simulation image,  
you can reduce the particle diameter to less than 1 mm.  
A warning window will pop up when you modify this.  
This will seriously impact memory consumption  
and carries the risk of crashing.  
If you want to continue, click Yes.  
A smaller particle diameter can make your picture look more realistic.  
You can open the rendering window to check the rendering effect.  

In the rendering window,  
you can see a new option in the rendering toolbar:  
Lock the rendering view.  
This allows you to edit the lighting in the 3D window  
while keeping the rendering window’s viewing angle unchanged.  
You can check the effect after lighting adjustment in the rendering window.  

Additionally, you can output multi-view rendering images.  
In the image properties, select custom view.  
At the bottom of the save options, an option for merging the whole scene is added.  
Click Open.  
The final rendering will be displayed.  
You can see the rendering image from each angle  
and the merged rendering image.  

After rendering is completed,  
we can also perform AI face-to-face integration.  
This is a highlight feature of this update.  
Click the magic wand button in the toolbar on the right side.  
Enter the AI model workshop.  
You will see the just-rendered image appear here automatically.  
Of course, you can also upload other pictures.  
Then, by setting gender, age, and race,  
randomly generating keywords or manually inputting keywords,  
you can automatically generate a reference image for face-to-face integration.  
Click Start Rendering and wait for the result.  
The rendered images will appear on the right side.  
You can also save the images.  

In addition, we can use real-time photos for AI face-to-face integration.  
After completing the 3D file in CLO,  
you can upload it to the original platform CloSat for one-stop writing.  

If you are a new user,  
you can visit our website and sign up for a new account.  

In CloSat,  
you can upload and share your 3D files with others anytime.  
Currently, you can upload multiple files simultaneously,  
and drag files directly to the workshop for more convenient operation.  

On the content page,  
you can browse uploaded files using the 3D reader.  
You can also see career pictures of the costume.  
You can mark and comment, which facilitates communication and coordination with other users.  

Additionally, you can use your 3D assets to create visual articles using the new Cross-Site function.  
In the visual reading board, you can match different content such as 3D clothing, fabric, clothes, color boards, etc. to showcase your design and concept.  
Users can check 3D clothing through the link and share the visual reading board with others via the link.  

The above covers the main functions of this update.  
Thank you for your warm response and support, which help us to continue improving and growing.  
We will also release separate function explanation videos later.  
So if you want to learn more about a specific function, please follow our official account.  

Thank you for watching.

chunks.title: CLO2024.1 New Feature Express: Brand New Features Released to Bring Your Creations to Life!
chunks.content: # CLO 2024.1 New Feature Express: Brand New Features Released to Bring Your Creations to Life! This document details the new features and updates introduced in CLO 2024.1, focusing on UI improvements, virtual model editing, pattern and material enhancements, rendering capabilities, AI integration, and the CloSat collaborative platform. It covers technical explanations, procedures, and examples relevant to clothing development workflows. --- ## User Interface (UI) Updates and Main Menu Changes This section explains the redesigned UI structure in CLO 2024.1, including new main menu options and improvements to file management and virtual model access. - The main menu now features three top-level options: **Produce**, **Connect**, and **Closet**. - **Closet** enables direct uploading of project files, clothing, or virtual models, including updated versions after modification. - The **Connect** menu contains the updated **Everywhere** function for file uploads, with a refreshed UI. - Under **Produce**, users find tools for coloring, material lists, and code checking. - The **Material** section includes a new material generator. - The **Virtual Model** section offers an updated virtual model editor and related functions. - A new virtual model folder named **Mantel Human** is added to the library window, allowing direct import into Closet. - Direct size editing in Closet is not supported; size and gender adjustments for Mantel Human models are done in the map window. --- ## Virtual Model Editor Enhancements This section covers updates to virtual model editing, including measurement line adjustments, size controls, and new virtual models. - Some faceless children virtual models have been updated under **Connect**. - The virtual model editor UI has been refined for better usability. - Users can single-click and drag measurement lines to adjust their position and value. - Right-click options allow resetting individual or all measurement positions. - Measurement values can be shown or hidden via the right editor. - Width size settings allow defining total widths (e.g., lower body) and linking width values with corresponding measurements so adjustments propagate naturally. - Controls now exist to adjust the width between thighs for male and female models, including thigh width and size. - Measurement lines on male models can be directly dragged for size modification. --- ## Pattern Editing and Seam Allowance Improvements This section details updates to 2D pattern editing, seam allowance handling, and panel extension tools. - Users can open previous versions of styles from the resource library and load them into the workspace. - In the 2D window, switching to black and white surface view enhances pattern editing. - The **Sewing Tool** now allows adding seam allowances that automatically get cut into seam allowance areas, applying to larger seam allowance types as well. - Seam allowance folding types can be changed via a shortcut and selected from a dropdown menu in the attribute editor. - Seam allowance transfer retains basic lines in the middle of the seam allowance for consistent flipping. - The **Extension Panel Tool** now supports extending symmetrical panels, though only outward; upper and lower line lengths can be edited independently.

chunks.title: CLO2024.1 New Feature Express: Brand New Features Released to Bring Your Creations to Life!
chunks.content: - The **Sewing Tool** now allows adding seam allowances that automatically get cut into seam allowance areas, applying to larger seam allowance types as well. - Seam allowance folding types can be changed via a shortcut and selected from a dropdown menu in the attribute editor. - Seam allowance transfer retains basic lines in the middle of the seam allowance for consistent flipping. - The **Extension Panel Tool** now supports extending symmetrical panels, though only outward; upper and lower line lengths can be edited independently. - Seam allowance folding can be toggled in the secondary selection window or through a convenient keyboard shortcut (single icon key next to the return key). - After sewing, seam allowances are visible on garments and editable as needed. --- ## Button and Model Library Management This section explains updates to button editing and organizing clothing models in the model library. - When selecting buttons, options to add face buttons and eye buttons appear; resizing the button automatically adjusts the eye button size. - Clothing models can be added to the model library by selecting the target group. - An **Automatic Label** button in the model library automatically tags panels to the correct category. - Missing tags can be manually assigned by selecting the component category and corresponding panel, then confirming. - Style and name updates for models are possible via right-click > Edit Style, allowing renaming and shrink chart modifications which update the original component’s name. --- ## Fabric and Material Enhancements: Wool and sRGB Support This section covers fabric texture and color improvements, including wool randomness control and sRGB color consistency. - A new option for wool fabric allows **random mixing of bone lines**, creating color randomness controlled by a slider or numerical input. - Wool direction can be adjusted via a slider or by entering values. - CLO now supports **sRGB format**, improving color consistency between Photoshop and CLO. - sRGB stickers created in Photoshop maintain color fidelity when imported into CLO and vice versa. - Example: Adding sRGB stickers to an inner top shirt maintains consistent color appearance across platforms. --- ## Sticker and Texture Improvements This section describes enhancements to sticker functionality, including texture matching, preset types, and automatic generation. - In the property editor, stickers on jeans now have a **"Use the same as the plant"** option, which applies the underlying fabric’s hairline texture to the sticker. - Adjusting the hairline intensity on the fabric also updates the sticker accordingly. - This option is available for transparent, 3D stickers, and other sticker types. - Stickers now support preset types such as **digital print**, **uniform**, **retrofitting**, and **gold**, with customizable gold color. - Mixing sticker presets with the plant applies all 3D stickers of the fabric. - Clicking a sticker in the object window initially shows only the texture picture. - The **Automatically Generate** button creates additional 3D stickers quickly; generated stickers can be stored separately. - The fabric (plant) can also use this automatic generation function.

chunks.content: - This option is available for transparent, 3D stickers, and other sticker types. - Stickers now support preset types such as **digital print**, **uniform**, **retrofitting**, and **gold**, with customizable gold color. - Mixing sticker presets with the plant applies all 3D stickers of the fabric. - Clicking a sticker in the object window initially shows only the texture picture. - The **Automatically Generate** button creates additional 3D stickers quickly; generated stickers can be stored separately. - The fabric (plant) can also use this automatic generation function. --- ## Color Flag System Enhancements This section explains the upgraded color flag system for flexible material and property adjustments. - Users can add flag colors that: - Adjust only material properties (e.g., color, texture, size). - Adjust all properties of related materials. - Flag colors can include ink and control sticker display. - Materials’ texture and physical properties can be edited independently via flag colors. - This system enables more flexible clothing viewing and editing during design workflows. --- ## Measurement Tool Optimizations This section highlights improvements in the measurement tool, including shortcut modes and measurement types. - Pressing shortcut key **P** switches between different measurement modes: - Color change mode. - Measuring length around a panel’s outer edge, similar to the free sewing tool. - Measuring straight line lengths inside panels. - Creating free straight lines inside and outside panels. - All measurement values are displayed in the object window for easy reference. --- ## Sticker Code Editing and Panel Inner Line Refitting This section covers improvements in sticker code sizing and panel code refitting. - The **Edit Code Tool** allows selecting a sticker and adjusting its code size via percentage or unit numbers. - Percentage adjustments facilitate easier scaling without exact size knowledge. - Inner line refitting on panels is now supported, enabling different methods of matching the sticker code to the garment. --- ## Full Mirror Mode and Multi-Size Viewing This section presents the new full mirror mode for better size comparison and observation. - **Full Mirror Mode** displays all garment sizes in one combined image. - Users can adjust the X-axis rotation to view garment angles and change spacing between sizes. - This mode assists in observing pressure and force distribution on garments across sizes. --- ## Rendering Enhancements This section describes new rendering features including style image completeness, eye color modification, particle diameter control, and multi-view rendering. - **Style Image Rendering** now shows chain and components, making style effect images more complete. - Virtual model eye color can be quickly modified via the **Sample Modifier** in the property editor, with options to reset or keep changes. - Simulation image particle diameter can be reduced to less than 1 mm for more realistic images. - A warning appears due to increased memory consumption and crash risk. - The rendering window has a new **Lock the Rendering View** option. - This allows editing lighting in the 3D window without changing the rendering window’s viewing angle.

chunks.title: CLO2024.1 New Feature Express: Brand New Features Released to Bring Your Creations to Life!
chunks.content: - Virtual model eye color can be quickly modified via the **Sample Modifier** in the property editor, with options to reset or keep changes. - Simulation image particle diameter can be reduced to less than 1 mm for more realistic images. - A warning appears due to increased memory consumption and crash risk. - The rendering window has a new **Lock the Rendering View** option. - This allows editing lighting in the 3D window without changing the rendering window’s viewing angle. - Multi-view rendering output is supported: - Users select **Custom View** in image properties. - A new option merges the whole scene into one image. - Rendering images from each angle and the merged scene are displayed. --- ## AI Face-to-Face Integration This section introduces AI-driven face integration features for rendered images and photos. - Accessible via the **Magic Wand** button in the toolbar. - Users enter the **AI Model Workshop**, where the latest rendered image appears automatically or can be replaced by uploaded photos. - Gender, age, and race can be set. - Keywords can be randomly generated or manually input to guide face generation. - Clicking **Start Rendering** generates reference images for face-to-face integration. - Rendered images appear on the right side and can be saved. - Real-time photos can also be used for AI face integration. - After completing 3D files in CLO, users can upload files to **CloSat** for one-stop collaboration. --- ## CloSat Platform: 3D File Sharing and Collaboration This section explains CloSat’s features for file sharing, browsing, commenting, and creating visual articles. - New users can sign up on the CloSat website. - Multiple files can be uploaded simultaneously by drag-and-drop. - Uploaded files can be browsed using a 3D reader. - Users can view costume career pictures and add marks or comments to facilitate team communication. - The **Cross-Site** function allows creating visual articles combining 3D clothing, fabrics, color boards, and more. - Visual reading boards can be shared via links, enabling easy distribution and presentation of designs. --- # Summary CLO 2024.1 introduces comprehensive updates across UI, virtual models, pattern editing, materials, rendering, and AI integration, enhancing the clothing development workflow. The new CloSat platform extends collaboration and sharing capabilities, supporting designers and teams

Mixing sticker presets with the plant applies all 3D stickers of the fabric. - Clicking a sticker in the object window initially shows only the texture picture. - The **Automatically Generate** button creates additional 3D stickers quickly; generated stickers can be stored separately. - The fabric (plant) can also use this automatic generation function. --- ## Color Flag System Enhancements This section explains the upgraded color flag system for flexible material and property adjustments. - Users can add flag colors that: - Adjust only material properties (e.g., color, texture, size). - Adjust all properties of related materials. - Flag colors can include ink and control sticker display. - Materials’ texture and physical properties can be edited independently via flag colors. - This system enables more flexible clothing viewing and editing during design workflows. --- ## Measurement Tool Optimizations This section highlights improvements in the measurement tool, including shortcut modes and measurement types. - Pressing shortcut key **P** switches between different measurement modes: - Color change mode. - Measuring length around a panel’s outer edge, similar to the free sewing tool. - Measuring straight line lengths inside panels. - Creating free straight lines inside and outside panels. - All measurement values are displayed in the object window for easy reference. --- ## Sticker Code Editing and Panel Inner Line Refitting This section covers improvements in sticker code sizing and panel code refitting. - The **Edit Code Tool** allows selecting a sticker and adjusting its code size via percentage or unit numbers. - Percentage adjustments facilitate easier scaling without exact size knowledge. - Inner line refitting on panels is now supported, enabling different methods of matching the sticker code to the garment. --- ## Full Mirror Mode and Multi-Size Viewing This section presents the new full mirror mode for better size comparison and observation. - **Full Mirror Mode** displays all garment sizes in one combined image. - Users can adjust the X-axis rotation to view garment angles and change spacing between sizes. - This mode assists in observing pressure and force distribution on garments across sizes. --- ## Rendering Enhancements This section describes new rendering features including style image completeness, eye color modification, particle diameter control, and multi-view rendering. - **Style Image Rendering** now shows chain and components, making style effect images more complete. - Virtual model eye color can be quickly modified via the **Sample Modifier** in the property editor, with options to reset or keep changes. - Simulation image particle diameter can be reduced to less than 1 mm for more realistic images. - A warning appears due to increased memory consumption and crash risk. - The rendering window has a new **Lock the Rendering View** option. - This allows editing lighting in the 3D window without changing the rendering window’s viewing angle. - Multi-view rendering output is supported: - Users select **Custom View** in image properties. - A new option merges the whole scene into one image. - Rendering images from each angle and the merged scene are displayed. --- ## AI Face-to-Face Integration This section introduces AI-driven face integration features for rendered images and photos. - Accessible via the **Magic Wand** button in the toolbar. - Users enter the **AI Model Workshop**, where the latest rendered image appears automatically or can be replaced by uploaded photos. - Gender, age, and race can be set. - Keywords can be randomly generated or manually input to guide face generation. - Clicking **Start Rendering** generates reference images for face-to-face integration. - Rendered images appear on the right side and can be saved. - Real-time photos can also be used for AI face integration. - After completing 3D files in CLO, users can upload files to **CloSat** for one-stop collaboration. --- ## CloSat Platform: 3D File Sharing and Collaboration This section explains CloSat’s features for file sharing, browsing, commenting, and creating visual articles. -
